target_customer: Gen Z and millennial pet owners in the San Francisco Bay Area who pay an annual membership
problem: Veterinary care is hard to access and impersonal; owners want preventative, personalized care with virtual and in-clinic options.
business_model: Annual membership (Dr. Treat One at $149 per year) plus pay-as-you-go visits ($85) and clinic services

founders.name: Rakesh Tondon
founders.background_notes: YC page lists no background. A search result says the idea came from his experience with his dog and that his wife Hetal Shah proposed it.

founders.name: Hetal Shah
previous_startups: Dr. Treat (YC page says it grew to two clinics and $9M ARR before being acquired in 2025)
founders.background_notes: Per YC page; began in advertising.

founders.name: Charlie Bowman
founders.background_notes: YC page lists no background; CTO title per Dealroom summary.

competitors.name: Modern Animal
competitors.what: Tech-enabled vet clinics also called One Medical for pets, in Los Angeles
competitors.funding_then: $13.5M seed led by Founders Fund and Upfront in October 2019

competitors.name: Small Door Veterinary
competitors.what: Membership based vet clinics in New York

technical_complexity.rationale: Operating clinics plus an app and telehealth is operations heavy rather than technically hard.

defensibility.rationale: Membership relationships and local clinics create stickiness, but Modern Animal and Small Door ran the same model earlier.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Unclear; the YC page says Dr. Treat was acquired in 2025 but no news source or acquirer was found.

market_need_then: Pet ownership surged in 2020 and 2021 and vet capacity was strained; an investor-funded set of premium membership clinics existed, showing willingness to pay in affluent markets.

brand_strength.rationale: Friendly, pet-themed name but no press on the brand itself; the tagline borrows One Medical and is shared by Modern Animal.

outcome_analysis: Dr. Treat opened its San Francisco clinic in 2022 and by Dealroom a second in Burlingame in early 2024, and sells memberships. The YC page claims an acquisition in 2025 after reaching $9M ARR, but no independent source or acquirer was found, so the outcome is uncertain. Funding figures conflict across sources.
notes: Funding unverified and conflicting: a company release reprinted by dvm360 (via search summary, not opened) says $10.5M seed in 2022; Dealroom shows an $11M seed in December 2023 at a $42M valuation led by EPIC Ventures; other trackers show $2M in December 2023. No round recorded. Directory status is Active while the YC founder bio for Hetal Shah says Dr. Treat was acquired in 2025; exit type left unknown. Founded year 2021 per YC page. Competitor Small Door date unconfirmed.
